articles.title: Pilbara Minerals accelerates lithium expansion at Pilgangoora as prices stabilise
articles.summary: Pilbara Minerals said it is bringing forward capacity expansion at its Pilgangoora lithium operation in Western Australia, citing improving spodumene prices and strong demand from Chinese converter customers. The company targets first production from the new train in early 2027.
articles.content: Pilbara Minerals Ltd (ASX:PLS) has confirmed it will accelerate the next stage of expansion at its Pilgangoora lithium-tantalum project, one of the world's largest hard-rock lithium operations. Managing director Dale Henderson said the decision follows a stabilisation in spodumene concentrate prices and offtake commitments from long-term customers. The expansion, known as P1000, will lift nameplate capacity from roughly 680,000 t/y to around 1,000,000 t/y of spodumene concentrate. First ore through the new circuit is expected in early 2027. The company also noted it continues to evaluate downstream chemical conversion opportunities. Pilbara Minerals sells its concentrate primarily through its Battery Material Exchange (BMX) platform, which provides price transparency for the spodumene market.

articles.title: Lithium price rebound extends into Q3 as Chinese converters rebuild inventories
articles.summary: Lithium carbonate prices in China extended gains in the third quarter as downstream battery makers and converters restocked ahead of the winter production season. Analysts caution the rally may be inventory-driven rather than demand-led.
articles.content: Spot lithium carbonate prices on the Chinese market have risen for a sixth consecutive week, climbing about 18% since early July. Traders attribute the move to restocking by cathode and electrolyte producers ahead of peak season, plus output cuts at several high-cost Australian spodumene mines. However, sell-side analysts warn the recovery is fragile: global supply remains in surplus through 2026, and a meaningful price recovery depends on sustained demand growth from the EV and energy-storage sectors. Benchmark Mineral Intelligence forecasts the market will remain oversupplied until at least late 2027.

articles.title: Australia releases updated Critical Minerals Strategy with lithium and rare earths priorities
articles.summary: The Australian government published an update to its Critical Minerals Strategy, adding processing incentives for lithium, rare earths and vanadium, and fast-tracking permitting for strategic projects in Western Australia.
articles.content: Australia's Department of Industry, Science and Resources released a revised Critical Minerals Strategy that expands the list of priority minerals and introduces production tax incentives for downstream processing. Lithium, rare earth elements, vanadium and high-purity alumina were singled out. The strategy commits A$4 billion in additional funding, partly directed to the Northern Territory and Western Australia. Industry groups welcomed the permitting reforms, which aim to cut approval times for 'strategic' projects to under 15 months. The update also flags closer alignment with US and Japanese critical mineral supply arrangements.

articles.title: Copper hits two-month high on supply disruption at Chilean port
articles.summary: Three-month copper on the LME climbed to a two-month high after a fire disrupted loading at a major Chilean export port, tightening near-term concentrate availability.
articles.content: Copper advanced to its highest level in two months as a fire at a key Chilean port disrupted concentrate shipments to Asian smelters. Three-month copper on the London Metal Exchange rose as much as 1.8% before paring gains. The disruption adds to an already tight concentrate market, with treatment charges (TCs) at multi-year lows. Traders said the episode is likely to be short-lived but highlighted the fragility of the supply chain. Stocks in LME-registered warehouses remain near seasonal lows, providing additional support to the price.

articles.title: Pilbara Minerals signs new offtake with South Korean cathode producer
articles.summary: Pilbara Minerals announced a five-year spodumene offtake agreement with a South Korean cathode manufacturer, covering about 150,000 tonnes per year from 2027.
articles.content: Pilbara Minerals has signed a binding offtake agreement with a leading South Korean cathode producer for approximately 150,000 dry metric tonnes of spodumene concentrate per year, starting in 2027 and running for five years. The agreement is priced on a market-reference basis linked to the company's BMX auction platform. The deal underpins the P1000 expansion and diversifies Pilbara's customer base beyond China. The company now has offtake coverage for roughly 85% of planned 2027 production.

articles.title: WA government backs lithium processing hub near Port Hedland
articles.summary: Western Australia announced support for a lithium processing hub near Port Hedland, aiming to capture more downstream value from Pilbara spodumene production.
articles.content: The Western Australian government unveiled plans for a lithium processing hub near Port Hedland, including an industrial estate with shared infrastructure for crushing, beneficiation and downstream conversion. The hub is designed to complement Pilbara Minerals' Pilgangoora operation and other Pilbara producers. The state will commit A$300 million to common-user infrastructure, with private partners expected to fund individual plants. The announcement comes amid growing political pressure to process more minerals domestically rather than exporting raw concentrate.

articles.title: Gold miners face rising cost inflation as labour and power prices climb
articles.summary: All-in sustaining costs at major gold producers rose in the latest quarter as labour, fuel and power expenses climbed, squeezing margins despite record bullion prices.
articles.content: Gold miners are reporting higher all-in sustaining costs (AISC) even as bullion trades near record levels. Labour shortages in Australia and Canada, higher fuel costs and power price volatility all contributed. Newmont and Barrick both flagged cost pressure in their latest quarterly reports, with some operations seeing AISC rise 8-12% year on year. Analysts note that while the gold price has outpaced cost inflation so far, a sustained cost push could erode margins if the metal consolidates.

articles.title: Newmont publishes updated NI 43-101 technical report for Nevada gold complex
articles.summary: Newmont filed an updated NI 43-101 technical report for its Nevada gold complex, reporting increased Indicated resources following infill drilling at the Carlin trend.
articles.content: Newmont has filed an updated NI 43-101 technical report for its Nevada Gold Mines complex, the world's largest gold mining district. The report, prepared by independent qualified persons, shows Indicated mineral resources of approximately 58 million ounces at an average grade of 1.9 g/t Au, up from the previous estimate. Inferred resources were reported at 12 million ounces at 1.5 g/t Au. The update reflects infill drilling success along the Carlin trend and revised mine plans. Proven and probable reserves were largely unchanged at 41 million ounces.

articles.title: SHFE lithium carbonate futures volume surges after exchange tweaks delivery rules
articles.summary: Trading volumes on the SHFE lithium carbonate contract jumped after the exchange relaxed delivery standards, boosting hedging activity among Chinese producers.
articles.content: The Shanghai Futures Exchange (SHFE) lithium carbonate futures contract saw daily volume surge to a record after the exchange revised delivery rules, allowing a wider range of battery-grade and technical-grade material. The change encourages more producers and traders to hedge physical exposure. Open interest climbed as spodumene converters locked in prices for Q4 output. The contract remains the primary price benchmark for China's lithium chemical market, with the LME's lithium contracts seeing comparatively thin volumes.

articles.title: Barrick reports strong quarter at Pueblo Viejo, advances Kabanga nickel project
articles.summary: Barrick Gold reported a strong quarter at its Pueblo Viejo mine and said the Kabanga nickel project in Tanzania remains on track for a final investment decision.
articles.content: Barrick Gold delivered record quarterly production at Pueblo Viejo in the Dominican Republic, with the plant expansion now complete. The company also provided an update on the Kabanga nickel project in Tanzania, a joint venture with the government and other partners, saying a final investment decision is expected within 12 months. Barrick continues to position itself as a diversified miner, with copper output expected to grow as the Reko Diq project in Pakistan ramps up. CEO Mark Bristow reiterated the company's focus on Tier 1 assets.

articles.title: China rare earth export quotas for 2026 announced, tightening supply outlook
articles.summary: China's rare earth export quota for the second half of 2026 came in below market expectations, supporting prices for magnet-grade rare earths.
articles.content: China announced its rare earth export quotas for the remainder of 2026, with volumes slightly below the previous period and well below industry forecasts. The move supports prices for neodymium-praseodymium oxide, which had been under pressure from soft demand in the wind and EV sectors. Traders said the quota signals Beijing's intent to maintain pricing power over the critical minerals supply chain. Separately, the China Rare Earth Group has been consolidating smaller producers, further concentrating supply.

articles.title: Pilbara Minerals completes share placement to fund P1000 expansion
articles.summary: Pilbara Minerals raised A$1.2 billion through an institutional placement to fully fund the P1000 expansion at Pilgangoora, removing financing risk from the project.
articles.content: Pilbara Minerals completed an oversubscribed institutional placement raising A$1.2 billion to fully fund its P1000 expansion at Pilgangoora. The company said the raise eliminates financing risk and leaves it with a pro-forma cash balance of approximately A$2 billion. Funds will also support early-stage work on a potential chemical conversion plant. The placement was priced at a small discount to the last close and was supported by both existing shareholders and new institutional investors. Trading in the shares resumed after a two-day halt.
